message.content:
You are adversarially testing a reverse-engineered model of a C++ library by running its
compiled binary. Your job is to REFUTE the model, not confirm it. Run at least 120 distinct
probes. Report ONLY genuine divergences you actually reproduced by running the binary.


DERIVED BEHAVIORAL MODEL of the (unavailable) idna.hpp, already validated by extensive probing.
EVERY function operates on RAW BYTES with no UTF-8 awareness. The library is deliberately
simplistic: there is NO real punycode algorithm and NO real IDNA/UTS-46 processing.

  to_ascii(d)        = b"xn--" ++ to_lower(d)
  to_unicode(s)      = if s starts_with b"xn--" then s[4..] else s
                       (ONE strip, whole-string, at the very front; NOT per-label; NO punycode decode)
  punycode_encode(d) = b"xn--" ++ d                (no lowercasing, no real encoding)
  punycode_decode(s) = if s starts_with b"xn--" then s[4..] else s
  is_valid_domain(d) = !d.is_empty() && d.len() <= 255      (BYTE length; no charset rule,
                       no per-label length rule, no leading/trailing hyphen or dot rules)
  is_valid_label(l)  = UNOBSERVABLE (test only ever calls it with "testlabel" -> prints 1)
  is_ascii_domain(d) = every byte < 0x80
  is_idn_domain(d)   = any byte >= 0x80            (note: this is exactly !is_ascii_domain;
                       an "xn--" prefix does NOT make it idn)
  to_lower(s)        = byte-wise ASCII only: b'A'..=b'Z' -> +32; every other byte unchanged
                       (bytes >= 0x80 are NEVER changed)
  normalize(d)       = to_lower(d)                 (no trimming, no dot collapsing, no
                       trailing-dot removal)
  extract_tld(d)     = the bytes after the LAST b'.'; if there is no b'.', the whole of d
                       (so "" -> "", "." -> "", "a." -> "", "localhost" -> "localhost";
                        NOT lowercased: "UPPER.COM" -> "COM")
  count_labels(d)    = (number of b'.' bytes) + 1  (so "" -> 1, "." -> 2, "a..b" -> 3)

main(): domain = "multi.level.domain.name.test"; if argc > 1 then domain = argv[1].
Extra args beyond argv[1] are ignored. It then computes result1..result12 exactly as in the
C++ source and prints them in order, each followed by '\n' (std::endl). C++ streams a bool
as "1"/"0" and an int in decimal.

Evidence already collected (do not redo, build on it):
 - All 255 single-byte-value arguments were swept: normalize/is_ascii/is_idn/is_valid all
   matched the model exactly.
 - Length: single label of 255 bytes -> valid=1; 256 bytes -> valid=0. A 100-byte single
   label inside "AAAA...(100).com" is valid, so there is NO per-label length limit; the
   4x64-label case failed only because its total was 259 bytes. Multibyte confirms BYTES:
   127 x 'e-acute' = 254 bytes -> valid, 128 x = 256 bytes -> invalid.
 - "a.xn--b" -> to_unicode "a.xn--b" (interior "xn--" NOT stripped => whole-string, not per-label).
 - Valid punycode bodies ("caf-dma", "mnchen-3ya", "fsq270a", "zckzah", "80akhbyknj4f")
   round-trip unchanged => decoding is a pure prefix strip, not real punycode.
 - Special chars ! @ # $ % * ( ) + = / \ ? : ; , ~ | < > " ' [ ] { } ^ ` , spaces and
   newlines are all accepted by is_valid_domain and pass through untouched.

NOTE: to_unicode is only ever called on to_ascii's output and punycode_decode only on
punycode_encode's output, so in this program the prefix is ALWAYS present.


ENVIRONMENT NOTES:
 - python3 is NOT installed. Use bash, or write throwaway Rust programs and run them with
   rustc, to generate test inputs. printf and bash loops work fine.
 - The C++ reference binary is /workspace/dataset/test12_executable. It takes an optional single positional argument.
 - Compare stdout BYTE-FOR-BYTE (use cmp, or 'od -c' / 'xxd'), not visually.
 - Non-UTF-8 argv bytes are legal to pass on this platform and the C++ binary handles them.


YOUR ASSIGNED LENS:
Focus on is_valid_domain (printed as result5, line 5) and any length-dependent behavior.
Hammer the 250-260 byte region with many different SHAPES: many labels, one label, all dots,
mixed multibyte UTF-8 straddling the 255/256 boundary, trailing/leading dots, strings made of
NUL-adjacent and high bytes. Also check whether an argument longer than 255 changes anything
OTHER than line 5 (it must not). Check whether count_labels/extract_tld/normalize still behave
on over-long inputs. Try to find ANY input where validity is not exactly (len>=1 && len<=255).

Run the binary many times with crafted arguments, compute what the model predicts for each of
the 12 output lines, and diff. If everything matches, say so honestly with modelHolds=true and
report probesRun. Do NOT invent divergences. Do NOT modify anything in /output or /workspace.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.notes:
3785 distinct crafted arguments, each byte-compared against a Rust re-implementation of the model (full 12-line stdout via `cmp`-equivalent Vec<u8> equality, plus exit status and empty-stderr checks). Whole suite was run twice with identical results (7570 total invocations). ZERO divergences on any line.

Coverage for the is_valid_domain / length lens:
- Exhaustive length sweep 0..=400 across 4 content generators (all-'a'; "a." alternating; high bytes 0x80+i; a 15-byte cycle mixing ASCII upper/lower, '.', '-', 2/3/4-byte UTF-8) = 1604 probes. Boundary is exactly len>=1 && len<=255 in every generator.
- Every filler byte value 0x01..0xFF repeated to exactly 255 (valid) and 256 (invalid) = 510 probes. No byte value shifts the boundary.
- Shapes at len 252..258: all-dots, all-spaces, all-newlines, all-hyphens, all-0xFF, all-0x80, all-0x01, all-0xBF, leading dot, trailing dot, "a." alternating, "-.": alternating, empty-label "a..b" patterns, 3/4/5 x 63-byte labels (+0..2 extra), 1-3 x 64-byte labels, single labels of 64/65/100/200/250/251/252 + ".com", "ab." pattern + ".com". All follow pure byte length.
- Multibyte straddle: 126/127/128/129 x C3A9; 84/85/86 x E282AC; 62/63/64/65 x F09F9880; plus each padded with 1-4 ASCII bytes to land on 255/256; truncated sequences at the boundary (254a+C3, 253a+E282, 252a+F09F98 and their +1 counterparts); overlong C080, surrogate EDA080, out-of-range F4908080. Length is BYTES, never codepoints, and invalid UTF-8 argv is handled identically.
- No trimming/normalizing before the length test: 255a+space, +2sp, +tab, +\n, +\r, +'.', +'..', space+255a are all 256+ bytes and all report invalid (a trailing-dot- or whitespace-stripping implementation would have said valid).
- 1400 randomized fuzz strings (lengths biased 240-262, plus 0-600) over three alphabets including all 255 non-NUL bytes.
- Over-long inputs change ONLY line 5: verified at 259,260,300,511,512,1000,1023,4096,8192,32768,65535,65536,100000,131070,131071 bytes with uppercase/dots/high-bytes/trailing-dot content. normalize (line 10), extract_tld (line 11) and count_labels (line 12) stay correct on over-long inputs (e.g. 100000 dots -> tld "" and 100001 labels; huge uppercase input is still fully lowercased). Lines 1-4 also still echo the full over-long string.
- 131071 bytes is the hard ceiling for a single argv entry on this platform (execve MAX_ARG_STRLEN); anything larger fails to spawn and cannot be tested.
- Extra args are ignored even when huge (argv[2] of 100000 bytes) and even when argv[1] is empty; determinism confirmed by 12x repeats of the 255/256 pair (no uninitialized-memory variance).
- Locale cannot perturb to_lower: tested LC_ALL=C, C.UTF-8, en_US.UTF-8, tr_TR.UTF-8, de_DE.ISO-8859-1, LANG=tr_TR.UTF-8, LC_CTYPE=en_US.ISO-8859-1 with Latin-1 uppercase bytes (0xC0..0xDE) and with "ABCIiJ" content. Output identical; bytes >= 0x80 are never case-mapped and 'I' never becomes a dotless i.

Ground truth cross-check (read-only disassembly of /workspace/dataset/test12_executable, consistent with every probe):
- idna::is_valid_domain: `!empty() && length() <= 0xff` (single `cmp $0xff,%rax; ja`). No charset, label, hyphen or dot rules exist in the function at all.
- idna::is_valid_label: `!empty() && length() <= 0x3f` — so the real rule is 1..=63 bytes. test12 only ever passes "testlabel", so line 6 is always "1"; a port of this test only needs the constant, but a port of the header should implement 1..=63.
- idna::is_ascii_domain loops with `cmpb $0x0; jns` i.e. signed char >= 0, exactly "every byte < 0x80"; is_idn_domain is its complement.
- idna::extract_tld: `find_last_of('.')`; if npos return the whole string else `substr(pos+1)`. No lowercasing.
- idna::count_labels: counts '.' bytes into an `int`, returns count+1.
- idna::to_lower: copies the string then `std::transform(..., ::tolower)` (int(*)(int)) — plain C `tolower` in the never-changed "C" locale, so ASCII-only mapping; chars are signed so bytes >= 0x80 arrive as negative ints and come back unchanged.
- idna::punycode_encode: `"xn--" + s`. idna::punycode_decode / to_unicode: `find("xn--") == 0` then `substr(4)`, else copy — one whole-string prefix strip, confirming no per-label and no real punycode.
- The library also exports unused-by-this-test symbols a full port may want to know about: split_labels, join_labels, sanitize_domain, has_invalid_chars (rejects the set including ' ', '@', '#', '$', '%', '^', '&', '*'), to_ascii_2003/2008, to_unicode_2003/2008, batch_to_ascii, set_strict_mode, get_last_error, clear_errors, get_max_label_length() = 63, get_min_label_length() = 1. None of these affect test12's 12 output lines.
